source_config.auto_flatten_all.a: A real JSON boolean (`true`/`false`); `check_bool` rejects a quoted `"true"` with 'Use the JSON literals true/false, not a quoted string'.

source_config.auto_flatten_all.q: Does auto_flatten_all make ingestion slower than named explode_columns?
source_config.auto_flatten_all.a: It recursively flattens every nested struct and explodes every array anywhere in the schema, which can produce a much larger row count (cartesian growth per array) than a scoped, named list — cost scales with how deeply/widely nested the actual payload is, not a fixed overhead.

source_config.auto_flatten_all.q: What happens if I set auto_flatten_all: true and also populate explode_columns?
source_config.auto_flatten_all.a: It only takes effect while `explode_columns` is absent or empty — a populated `explode_columns` list wins and scopes flattening to just those named columns, regardless of `auto_flatten_all`. See docs/02 §6 table.

source_config.capture_technical_metadata.q: What happens if capture_technical_metadata is not set at all?
source_config.capture_technical_metadata.a: Its schema default is `null`/unset (no default shown in the schema), meaning the framework's file-provenance columns and `__framework_ingestion_timestamp_utc` are not populated. This is distinct from an explicit `false` only in that omitting vs. `false` both leave it off.

source_config.capture_technical_metadata.q: Is capture_technical_metadata a boolean or a string flag?
source_config.capture_technical_metadata.a: A real JSON boolean; `check_bool` flags a quoted `"true"`/`"false"` as invalid — 'expected a boolean (true/false in JSON)'.

source_config.capture_technical_metadata.q: Does turning on capture_technical_metadata add noticeable overhead?
source_config.capture_technical_metadata.a: Negligible — it only adds four metadata columns (`__framework_source_file_name`, `_size`, `_modification_time`, `_metadata_headers`) and a timestamp column per row; no extra scan or shuffle is introduced.

source_config.capture_technical_metadata.q: Why does my CDC pipeline fail at startup complaining about sequence_by_column when this is off?
source_config.capture_technical_metadata.a: With `capture_technical_metadata` set `false`, `__framework_ingestion_timestamp_utc` never gets created, and that column is the CDC default sequencing column — so `dlt.apply_changes` has nothing to sequence by. Either re-enable this attribute, or set `target_config.sequence_by_column` to a real column explicitly.

source_config.column_normalization.case.q: What case does column_normalization use if I don't set the case field?
source_config.column_normalization.case.a: It defaults to `lower` per the JSON schema, matching pre-v1.3.0 behaviour byte-for-byte, but only takes effect when `column_normalization.enabled` is `true`.

source_config.column_normalization.case.q: What are the exact allowed values for column_normalization.case?
source_config.column_normalization.case.a: Only `lower`, `preserve`, or `upper` (`ALLOWED_COLUMN_NORMALIZATION_CASES`); any other string fails with the standard allowed-values error from `check_string`.

source_config.column_normalization.case.q: Does choosing preserve or upper cost more than the default lower?
source_config.column_normalization.case.a: Negligible — only the case-fold step of the per-column name transform changes; character normalization (whitespace trim, non-alphanumeric replacement, `_` collapsing) always runs regardless of `case`.

source_config.column_normalization.case.q: Can case: preserve produce two columns that collide after normalization?
source_config.column_normalization.case.a: Collision detection always runs on the lowercased projection of the produced names regardless of `case`, so `Order_ID` and `order_id` are still caught even under `preserve`/`upper`. A collision raises: 'normalization produced duplicate column names ... Rename one of the source columns, or use schema_config_path for explicit renaming instead.' See docs/02 §8.

source_config.column_normalization.enabl.q: Is column normalization on by default if I set case but not enabled?
source_config.column_normalization.enabl.a: No. As of v1.4.0, `enabled` defaults to `false` and is the only switch — an absent object, absent key, or explicit `false` all mean off, even if `case` is supplied alongside it. Omitting the attribute is not the same as it being truthy; check the default explicitly.

source_config.column_normalization.enabl.q: Do I write enabled as true/false or as a quoted flag?
source_config.column_normalization.enabl.a: A real JSON boolean; a quoted string fails `check_bool`'s type check with 'Use the JSON literals true/false, not a quoted string.'

source_config.column_normalization.enabl.q: Is there a runtime cost to enabling column_normalization?
source_config.column_normalization.enabl.a: Negligible per-column string transform (trim, character replace, case-fold) plus one collision check on the lowercased projection of all output names — not a data scan or shuffle.

source_config.column_normalization.enabl.q: I used the old normalize_column_names flag before — does it still work?
source_config.column_normalization.enabl.a: No — `source_config.normalize_column_names` is REJECTED as of v1.4.0, not silently ignored, because an ignored `true` would silently switch renaming off and let raw special-character column names hit the Delta target. Migrate `{"normalize_column_names": true}` to `{"column_normalization": {"enabled": true}}`. See docs/02 §8 migration table.

source_config.data_standardization_sql.q: What happens if data_standardization_sql is left out?
source_config.data_standardization_sql.a: It is fully optional; the validator returns immediately when it is `None`, so no standardization expressions run and the ingested columns pass through as read (after explode/dedup).

source_config.data_standardization_sql.q: Can I put a SELECT or a semicolon inside a data_standardization_sql entry?
source_config.data_standardization_sql.a: No — each entry is a restricted per-column expression that must end `AS <column>`; the grammar forbids `SELECT`/`FROM`/`JOIN`/`UNION`/`WHERE`, any DML/DDL keyword, and semicolons. An empty/blank entry is also rejected: '`<path>[<index>]`: must not be empty'.

source_config.data_standardization_sql.q: Does adding many standardization expressions slow down ingestion noticeably?
source_config.data_standardization_sql.a: Each expression is a plain column-level `withColumn`/`select` transform evaluated once per surviving row (after dedup, per docs/02 §7) — cost scales roughly linearly with expression count and complexity, not a separate scan.

source_config.data_standardization_sql.q: In what order does data_standardization_sql run relative to remove_dups and column_normalization?
source_config.data_standardization_sql.a: It runs after explode/auto-flatten and after `remove_dups`, and after `column_normalization`'s renames — so expressions must reference the already-normalized column names, not the raw source names. See docs/02 §7 and §8 'Ordering'.

source_config.dedup_watermark.delay_thre.q: What if I set remove_dups: true but skip delay_threshold?
source_config.dedup_watermark.delay_thre.a: If you supply the `dedup_watermark` block at all, `delay_threshold` is required alongside `event_time_column` — omitting it fails with 'is required but was missing or empty'. If you omit the whole `dedup_watermark` block, dedup runs with unbounded state instead (no error, just a runtime WARNING).

source_config.dedup_watermark.delay_thre.q: What format does delay_threshold expect — a number of seconds or an interval string?
source_config.dedup_watermark.delay_thre.a: A Spark interval string like `"2 hours"` or `"30 minutes"`, not a bare number; it is validated only as a non-empty string, so a malformed interval is not caught until Spark's `withWatermark` call at runtime.

source_config.dedup_watermark.delay_thre.q: Does a longer delay_threshold cost more memory in the dedup state store?
source_config.dedup_watermark.delay_thre.a: Yes — a larger threshold retains more historical rows in dedup state before they age out, trading memory/state size against tolerance for late-arriving duplicates. A shorter threshold bounds memory tighter but risks treating a late duplicate as new.

source_config.dedup_watermark.delay_thre.q: Does dedup_watermark do anything if remove_dups is false?
source_config.dedup_watermark.delay_thre.a: No — it is rejected outright at onboarding when `remove_dups` is not `true`: 'only meaningful alongside remove_dups: true, but remove_dups is not enabled for this source'. It configures nothing on its own. See docs/02 §7.

source_config.dedup_watermark.event_time.q: Is event_time_column optional if delay_threshold is set?
source_config.dedup_watermark.event_time.a: No — both are required together whenever `dedup_watermark` is present; missing `event_time_column` fails with 'is required but was missing or empty' regardless of `delay_threshold` being set.

source_config.dedup_watermark.event_time.q: Does event_time_column need to reference the raw source column name or the normalized one?
source_config.dedup_watermark.event_time.a: It must name a TIMESTAMP column on the DataFrame at the point dedup runs, which is after explode/auto-flatten and after column normalization — so use the post-normalization name if `column_normalization` is enabled.

source_config.dedup_watermark.event_time.q: Does choosing event_time_column affect ingestion throughput?
source_config.dedup_watermark.event_time.a: Negligible in itself — it only feeds Spark's `withWatermark(...)` call, which bounds state rather than adding a scan. The real cost driver is `delay_threshold`, not which column is chosen.

source_config.dedup_watermark.event_time.q: What happens on a batch (non-streaming) source with dedup_watermark configured?
source_config.dedup_watermark.event_time.a: On a batch source, `dropDuplicates` is a plain shuffle with no state to bound, so `dedup_watermark` — if present — is simply ignored (logged at INFO), not an error. See docs/02 §7.

source_config.explode_columns.q: What is the difference between not setting explode_columns and setting it to an empty list?
source_config.explode_columns.a: This distinction is load-bearing: an absent key (or explicit `null`) is a schema-preserving pass-through — nothing is exploded. `"explode_columns": []` (present and empty) auto-flattens every nested struct and explodes every array recursively, equivalent to `auto_flatten_all: true`. Getting this backwards changes production row counts, not just column shapes. See docs/02 §6.

source_config.explode_columns.q: Can I list a column that is a plain scalar, not a struct or array?
source_config.explode_columns.a: The onboarding validator only checks it is a list of strings; a listed column that resolves to neither a struct nor an array at runtime raises `FrameworkConfigError` when the pipeline actually runs, since onboarding has no access to the source's real schema.

source_config.explode_columns.q: Does naming specific explode_columns cost less than auto_flatten_all?
source_config.explode_columns.a: Yes in general — a populated list scopes struct-flatten/array-explode treatment to only the named top-level columns, versus `auto_flatten_all`/empty-list which processes every nested struct and array anywhere in the schema recursively.

source_config.explode_columns.q: What happens when an array<struct<...>> column is named in explode_columns?
source_config.explode_columns.a: It is exploded first, then its resulting struct element is flattened in the same step — one entry handles both the array-explode and the struct-flatten for that column. See docs/02 §6 table.

source_config.explode_mode.q: What if explode_mode is left unset in the onboarding form?
source_config.explode_mode.a: This is a form-only convenience field (not a real spec key — it does not appear in `source_config`'s allowed keys); its default `absent` simply means the form omits `explode_columns` entirely, giving a schema-preserving pass-through.

source_config.explode_mode.q: Is explode_mode itself written into the JSON spec?
source_config.explode_mode.a: No — it only controls how the form writes `explode_columns`: `absent` omits the key, `empty` writes `explode_columns: []`, `named` writes the list you supply. Check `all_attribute_paths.txt`/the schema for the real spec key, which is `source_config.explode_columns`.

source_config.explode_mode.q: Does picking empty vs named in explode_mode change ingestion cost?
source_config.explode_mode.a: Yes, indirectly — `empty` triggers the same recursive flatten-everything behaviour as `auto_flatten_all`, which is more expensive than `named`, which scopes the flatten/explode to only the columns you list.

source_config.explode_mode.q: Why does the form hide explode_mode sometimes?
source_config.explode_mode.a: It only applies to certain source/format configurations (e.g. it is meaningful mainly for `json`/nested sources); the form hides it when it is not relevant to the current source_type/format combination selected.

source_config.file_pattern.q: What happens if file_pattern is not set on an Auto Loader source?
source_config.file_pattern.a: No `pathGlobFilter` option is applied at all, so every file under `path` matching Auto Loader's own format-detection rules is picked up — there is no implicit filtering default.

No — despite looking like it should, `file_pattern` always maps to Spark's generic `pathGlobFilter` option, for every format, not to `cloudFiles.fileNamePattern`. Auto Loader rejects any `cloudFiles.`-prefixed key outside its closed whitelist with `CF_UNKNOWN_OPTION_KEYS_ERROR`, which is exactly why the framework never emits that spelling.

source_config.file_pattern.q: Does a broad glob in file_pattern slow down file discovery?
source_config.file_pattern.a: `pathGlobFilter` is applied by the underlying file source during listing, so a narrower pattern reduces the file set Auto Loader has to consider each trigger — a very broad pattern (e.g. `*`) has effectively no filtering benefit over omitting it.

source_config.file_pattern.q: Can reader_options override my file_pattern setting?
source_config.file_pattern.a: Yes — `reader_options` is applied after `file_pattern`'s `pathGlobFilter` option in `_apply_common_autoloader_options`, so a colliding key in `reader_options` silently overrides it. Keys are written verbatim with no collision warning.

source_config.filter_condition.q: What happens if source_config.filter_condition is left unset?
source_config.filter_condition.a: No filter is applied after the read -- the whole source table (after any task_run_id_column narrowing) flows into matching, unmodified. There is no default filter.

source_config.filter_condition.q: How do I substitute a date literal into source_config.filter_condition safely?
source_config.filter_condition.a: Use a bare `${param}` placeholder without surrounding quotes, e.g. `load_date = ${run_date}` -- `substitute_dynamic_parameters` already supplies the quotes for a string parameter, so writing `load_date = '${run_date}'` becomes `load_date = ''2024-01-01''`, a ParseException. It also supports `{{catalog}}`/`{{env}}` template variables, resolved at onboarding time.

source_config.filter_condition.q: Does source_config.filter_condition reduce the cost of the reconciliation source read?
source_config.filter_condition.a: Yes -- it is applied right after the read (and after task_run_id_column narrowing), so a selective filter shrinks the row count that reaches the Phase 1 fingerprint and the Phase 2 hash-key join for the source side.

source_config.filter_condition.q: How do I re-run reconciliation over an ad-hoc historical window using source_config.filter_condition?
source_config.filter_condition.a: Add `${start_date}`/`${end_date}` placeholders in `filter_condition`, change the root `pipeline_parameters`, then re-run onboarding with `action_type=UPDATE` (CREATE/UPDATE/VALIDATE_ONLY are the accepted values) and run the job -- there is no job widget that overrides these dates directly.

source_config.format.q: What error do I get if format is missing on an autoloader flow?
source_config.format.a: Onboarding rejects it: `source_config.format: is required but was missing or empty`, since `format` is required whenever `source_type` is `autoloader`.

source_config.format.q: Are format values case-sensitive, e.g. CSV vs csv?
source_config.format.a: The validator only checks it is a non-empty string — there is no enum restriction in `spec_validator.py` — but it is passed verbatim as `cloudFiles.format`, so it must match Auto Loader's own expected lowercase values (e.g. `csv`, `json`, `parquet`).

source_config.format.q: Does the choice of format materially change ingestion cost?
source_config.format.a: Yes — `parquet` carries its own schema and needs no extra type inference, while `csv`/`json` need `reader_options` (e.g. `cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes`) to behave predictably, and JSON's nested structure adds explode/flatten cost downstream if configured.

source_config.format.q: Why did every column come back as a string when I used csv?
source_config.format.a: `cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes` was not set for the `csv` reader. Add `"cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes": "true"` to `reader_options`, or declare a `schema_config_path` for explicit types.

source_config.hash_precomputed.q: What happens if source_config.hash_precomputed is left unset?
source_config.hash_precomputed.a: It behaves as `false`: the engine computes `__framework_hash_key` (SHA-256 over `match_keys` in declared order) and `__framework_hash_value` (SHA-256 over `compare_columns`, alphabetically sorted) now, from raw columns, overwriting anything already present under those names.

source_config.hash_precomputed.q: Is hash_precomputed an instruction to precompute hashes?
source_config.hash_precomputed.a: No -- it is an assertion, not an instruction. `true` declares the hashes were ALREADY computed upstream when the table was materialized; it never causes anything to be precomputed. `false` (default) computes both columns now. See docs/07 section 9.

source_config.hash_precomputed.q: Does hash_precomputed true make reconciliation cheaper?
source_config.hash_precomputed.a: Yes, when the precondition holds -- it skips a full hash pass over this side's rows, and clustering the table on `__framework_hash_key` makes the join cheap at scale. It only helps for a framework-managed table already materialized by a CDC-dispatched flow with `generate_hash_columns` on.

source_config.hash_precomputed.q: What happens if hash_precomputed is true but the table's columns don't actually match this flow's match_keys/compare_columns?
source_config.hash_precomputed.a: Nothing errors at match time -- the hashes simply never match, and every row reports as VALUE_DRIFT or missing, silently wrong. The precondition is that the upstream flow's `primary_keys` equal this flow's `match_keys` and its comparison columns equal `compare_columns`; onboarding does reject `hash_precomputed: true` when `type` is not `table`. See docs/07 section 9.

source_config.json_string_columns.q: What happens if json_string_columns is left out on a Parquet source with JSON-in-a-string columns?
source_config.json_string_columns.a: It is fully optional; when absent, no `from_json` parsing runs on any string column, so a JSON document sitting in a STRING column stays an opaque string and is never flattened.

source_config.json_string_columns.q: What are the two accepted shapes for a json_string_columns entry?
source_config.json_string_columns.a: Either a bare column-name string (or `{"column": "col"}`), or `{"column": "col", "schema_ddl": "struct<...>"}` — the recommended, fully deterministic form. Listing the same column twice is rejected at onboarding: 'column '<col>' is listed more than once'.

source_config.json_string_columns.q: Is there a runtime cost difference between supplying schema_ddl and omitting it?
source_config.json_string_columns.a: Omitting `schema_ddl` falls back to Databricks' inferring `from_json`, which persists the inferred schema under a `schemaLocationKey` in the checkpoint — extra bookkeeping the explicit `schema_ddl` form avoids, since that form is deterministic with no inference step.

source_config.json_string_columns.q: Can I use the no-schema_ddl shorthand on a materialized_view or batch_table target?
source_config.json_string_columns.a: No — the no-`schema_ddl` shorthand only works on a streaming DataFrame; on a batch/materialized source it raises `FrameworkConfigError`: 'schema inference via from_json's schemaLocationKey requires a streaming source with a checkpoint. Supply an explicit schema_ddl...'. Always supply `schema_ddl` for `batch_table`/`materialized_view` targets. See docs/02 §6.

source_config.landing_retention_policy.a.q: Is archive_path required when clean_source is archive?
source_config.landing_retention_policy.a.a: No, never — not even for `clean_source: archive`. An empty or absent `archive_path` degrades the whole policy to `off` with a runtime WARNING, not a validation error. This was a deliberate v1.3.0 relaxation so an operator can pause archiving without deleting the block.

source_config.landing_retention_policy.a.q: What does the log say when archive_path is blank under clean_source: archive?
source_config.landing_retention_policy.a.a: 'landing_retention_policy.clean_source='archive' but archive_path is empty/absent -- degrading to clean_source='off': NO retention or cleanup action will be taken for this source.' It maps to `cloudFiles.cleanSource.moveDestination` only when non-empty.

source_config.landing_retention_policy.a.q: Does setting archive_path add overhead to every micro-batch?
source_config.landing_retention_policy.a.a: It only adds a file-move operation for files Auto Loader has already ingested and committed — a per-committed-file cost, not a per-trigger scan cost; negligible relative to the ingestion read itself.

source_config.landing_retention_policy.a.q: What happens if I leave archive_path set but change clean_source to delete?
source_config.landing_retention_policy.a.a: It is silently ignored, not flagged — `clean_source: delete` deletes by age alone and never reads `archive_path`, so a stray leftover value from an earlier `archive` configuration is an unused sibling field, not a misconfiguration. See docs/02 §2.

source_config.landing_retention_policy.c.q: What happens if clean_source is omitted?
source_config.landing_retention_policy.c.a: It defaults to `off`, which emits no `cloudFiles.cleanSource*` option at all — this is already Auto Loader's own default, so omitting it is byte-for-byte equivalent to the framework not setting the option.

source_config.landing_retention_policy.c.q: What are the only legal values for clean_source?
source_config.landing_retention_policy.c.a: `archive`, `delete`, or `off` (`ALLOWED_CLEAN_SOURCE_MODES`); any other string fails `check_string`'s allowed-values check.

source_config.landing_retention_policy.c.q: Which clean_source mode is cheapest at runtime?
source_config.landing_retention_policy.c.a: `off` is free (no option is even sent). `delete` is a metadata-only removal by age. `archive` costs a physical file move per committed file to `archive_path` — negligible per-file but scales with ingestion volume.

source_config.landing_retention_policy.c.q: Can I set landing_retention_policy.clean_source on a zerobus source?
source_config.landing_retention_policy.c.a: No — it is rejected at onboarding for any `source_type` other than `autoloader`/`asn1`: 'only applicable to source_type 'autoloader'/'asn1' (Auto Loader file ingestion), but this flow's source_type is 'zerobus''. A Zerobus stream reads an existing Delta table, so there is no landing zone to clean. See docs/02 §2.

source_config.landing_retention_policy.r.q: What retention_days value applies if I don't set it?
source_config.landing_retention_policy.r.a: It defaults to `7` (`DEFAULT_LANDING_RETENTION_DAYS` in `ingestion/readers.py`) — not zero, and not Auto Loader's own untouched default. A spec relying on the old implicit behaviour must now set it explicitly.

source_config.landing_retention_policy.r.q: Can retention_days be a decimal or a string like '7d'?
source_config.landing_retention_policy.r.a: No — it must be a real JSON integer `>= 0`; `check_int` also rejects a JSON boolean (Python's `bool` subclasses `int`) even though it type-checks as one.

It is legal and means 'no age threshold at all' — a file becomes eligible for archive/delete the moment Auto Loader commits it (`cloudFiles.cleanSource.retentionDuration = '0 days'`), which is the most aggressive, not a disabled, setting.

source_config.landing_retention_policy.r.q: Does retention_days matter if clean_source is off?
source_config.landing_retention_policy.r.a: No — when `clean_source` resolves to `off` (explicit or degraded from a blank `archive_path`), no `cloudFiles.cleanSource*` option is emitted at all, so `retention_days` is never read. See docs/02 §2.

source_config.max_bytes_per_trigger.q: What happens if max_bytes_per_trigger is not set on a zerobus source?
source_config.max_bytes_per_trigger.a: No `maxBytesPerTrigger` option is applied at all — the reader lets Delta's streaming source use its own default micro-batch sizing with no throttle from the framework.

source_config.max_bytes_per_trigger.q: What format does max_bytes_per_trigger expect — a plain number or a suffixed string?
source_config.max_bytes_per_trigger.a: A string like `"1g"`, matching Spark's own `maxBytesPerTrigger` option format (a size string with a unit suffix); it is validated only as a non-empty string, so an invalid unit is not caught until the stream starts.

source_config.max_bytes_per_trigger.q: Does max_bytes_per_trigger help control ingestion cost spikes?
source_config.max_bytes_per_trigger.a: Yes — it throttles how much data each micro-batch reads (`maxBytesPerTrigger`), which is exactly its purpose: bounding per-trigger read volume for a Zerobus/Delta streaming source to smooth compute and avoid oversized batches.

source_config.max_bytes_per_trigger.q: Does max_bytes_per_trigger apply to autoloader sources too?
source_config.max_bytes_per_trigger.a: It is documented and implemented only for the `zerobus` reader (`read_zerobus_source`), not `read_autoloader_source`; the equivalent Auto Loader throttle would be a different `reader_options` key like `maxFilesPerTrigger`, passed through separately.

source_config.path.q: What if source_config.path is missing on an autoloader flow?
source_config.path.a: Onboarding rejects it: `source_config.path: is required but was missing or empty`, since it is required whenever `source_type` is `autoloader` (and also for `asn1`).

source_config.path.q: Why must path always end with a trailing slash?
source_config.path.a: A path that looks like a file (no trailing slash) makes Auto Loader watch the parent directory instead of the intended one — always end with `/` to point at the actual incoming directory, e.g. `/Volumes/{{catalog}}/landing/orders/{{env}}/incoming/`.

source_config.path.q: Does mixing archived and incoming files in the same path directory slow things down?
source_config.path.a: It is worse than a performance issue — the docs warn it makes retention rules dangerous, since `landing_retention_policy` acts on the same directory Auto Loader reads from. Point `path` at a dedicated `incoming/` directory.

source_config.path.q: My pipeline update reports SUCCESS but wrote zero rows — why?
source_config.path.a: Most often `path` does not match where files actually land, especially when `source_zip_handling.target_volume_path` points somewhere else. The onboarding validator does not cross-check `path` against `target_volume_path` — confirm the extraction target and `path` are the same directory yourself.

source_config.read_mode.q: What is the default for source_config.read_mode if omitted?
source_config.read_mode.a: `batch` -- `ALLOWED_READ_MODES = {"batch", "streaming"}` and the sample in docs/07 shows `"batch"` as the baseline; the validator only runs its allowed-values/mode check when the key is present, but the runtime treats an absent value as batch.

source_config.read_mode.q: Are there only two legal values for source_config.read_mode?
source_config.read_mode.a: Yes -- `batch` or `streaming`; any other string fails `check_string`'s allowed-values check.

source_config.read_mode.q: Is streaming read_mode more expensive than batch for the reconciliation source?
source_config.read_mode.a: Streaming runs under `trigger(availableNow=True)` in job mode -- it processes everything currently available across as many micro-batches as needed then stops, matching a bounded job run; it needs a checkpoint (`checkpoint_root` widget) so it costs more state management than a plain batch read, which has none.

source_config.read_mode.q: Can source_config.read_mode be streaming when execution_mode is pipeline?
source_config.read_mode.a: No -- rejected on presence: 'streaming' is not supported when execution_mode is 'pipeline'/'pipeline_audit_only'. The in-pipeline comparison is a whole-snapshot batch classification, and a stream-static join supports only inner/left_outer, which cannot express MISSING_IN_SOURCE. Use `batch`, or set `execution_mode` to `job`.

source_config.reader_options.q: What happens if reader_options is left empty or absent for a CSV source?
source_config.reader_options.a: No extra `.option(key, value)` calls are made beyond `cloudFiles.format`/`schemaLocation` (and evolution/retention/file_pattern if set) — for `csv` specifically this typically means no header handling or type inference, so every column may arrive as a string.

source_config.reader_options.q: Are reader_options keys and values validated against real Spark option names?
source_config.reader_options.a: No — `check_dict_of_str` only verifies it is an object of string keys to string values; a typo'd key is written verbatim to the reader and becomes a silently ignored option, not an onboarding or runtime error.

source_config.reader_options.q: Can reader_options be used to control micro-batch throughput?
source_config.reader_options.a: Yes, e.g. `maxFilesPerTrigger` in `reader_options` throttles files per Auto Loader trigger the same way `max_bytes_per_trigger` does for Zerobus — this is a direct passthrough, so any Spark reader option is available at the cost of one `.option()` call per entry.

source_config.reader_options.q: What happens if a key in reader_options collides with file_pattern or schema_evolution_mode?
source_config.reader_options.a: `reader_options` is applied after `file_pattern` (`pathGlobFilter`) and after `schema_evolution_mode` (`cloudFiles.schemaEvolutionMode`) are set on the reader, so a colliding key in `reader_options` overrides both silently. See `ingestion/readers.py::_apply_common_autoloader_options`.

source_config.remove_dups.q: What happens if remove_dups is not set?
source_config.remove_dups.a: It defaults to `false` — no deduplication runs, and duplicate rows from the source (e.g. reprocessed files) pass straight through unchanged.

source_config.remove_dups.q: Is remove_dups a boolean or should I quote it?
source_config.remove_dups.a: A real JSON boolean; `check_bool` rejects a quoted `"true"` as invalid, requiring the literal `true`/`false`.

source_config.remove_dups.q: What is the cost of enabling remove_dups on a large streaming source?
source_config.remove_dups.a: Without a `dedup_watermark`, `dropDuplicates` keeps state for every distinct row seen since the stream started, forever — this is unbounded and will eventually degrade or fail a long-running pipeline. Set `dedup_watermark` to bound the state.

source_config.remove_dups.q: Which row survives when remove_dups collapses a duplicate group?
source_config.remove_dups.a: Spark gives no ordering guarantee, so the surviving row's `__framework_source_file_name`/`__framework_ingestion_timestamp_utc` is an arbitrary pick among the duplicates. A flow needing a deterministic 'keep earliest/latest' rule should use an SCD strategy or windowed `transformation_sql` instead. See docs/02 §7.

source_config.schema_config_path.q: What happens if schema_config_path is not set?
source_config.schema_config_path.a: It is fully optional; when absent, no external casts/nullability/comments/renames are applied — columns keep whatever type Auto Loader infers (or the native schema for parquet/Zerobus).

source_config.schema_config_path.q: Can schema_config_path point to a directory instead of a specific file?
source_config.schema_config_path.a: Yes — if it points to a directory, FlowX automatically resolves and loads the most recently modified file in that directory, so you do not need to hardcode a filename that changes over time.

source_config.schema_config_path.q: Is there a validation cost to using schema_config_path at onboarding time?
source_config.schema_config_path.a: Onboarding only checks it is a non-empty, required-when-present string — the referenced file's own shape is validated later, when it is actually loaded at pipeline graph-definition time, since onboarding has no Volume/workspace file access of its own.

source_config.schema_config_path.q: Does schema_config_path run before or after column_normalization?
source_config.schema_config_path.a: Its renames apply before column normalization — normalization runs immediately after the raw source read and after `schema_config_path`'s renames, so every downstream reference (explode_columns, data_standardization_sql, dq_config expressions) uses the post-normalization name. See docs/02 §8 'Ordering'.

source_config.schema_evolution_mode.q: What schema evolution mode applies if I never set schema_evolution_mode?
source_config.schema_evolution_mode.a: The attribute has no schema default listed and the check only runs `if evolution_mode:` truthy at runtime, so leaving it unset means no `cloudFiles.schemaEvolutionMode` option is set at all, and Auto Loader falls back to its own native default behaviour.

source_config.schema_evolution_mode.q: What are the exact legal values for schema_evolution_mode?
source_config.schema_evolution_mode.a: `addNewColumns`, `addNewColumnsWithTypeWidening`, `rescue`, `failOnNewColumns`, or `none` (`ALLOWED_SCHEMA_EVOLUTION_MODES`); an unsupported value also raises `FrameworkConfigError: Unsupported schema_evolution_mode: <value>` at the reader itself, in addition to the onboarding check.

source_config.schema_evolution_mode.q: Does rescue mode add processing cost compared to addNewColumns?
source_config.schema_evolution_mode.a: Not documented as materially different in cost — `rescue` redirects unparseable rows/unknown columns to `_rescued_data` rather than failing the stream, which is a routing decision, not an extra scan.

source_config.schema_evolution_mode.q: What happens with failOnNewColumns if the upstream source adds a column?
source_config.schema_evolution_mode.a: The stream immediately stops ingestion the moment a new column is detected — this is the strictest mode and is the opposite of `rescue`, which instead redirects the surprise data to `_rescued_data` and keeps running. See docs/02 'Schema Evolution Policies'.

source_config.schema_location.q: What happens if I omit schema_location for an autoloader flow?
source_config.schema_location.a: It is auto-derived: the loader defaults it to `/Volumes/<target_catalog>/landing/_schemas/<target_table>/` before the required-field check runs, using this flow's own `target_catalog`/`target_table` — so omitting it in practice is not an onboarding failure even though the schema marks it required.

source_config.schema_location.q: Can two flows share the same schema_location?
source_config.schema_location.a: No — give every flow its own schema location. Sharing one between flows corrupts both schemas, since Auto Loader persists the inferred schema and evolution history there per-stream.

source_config.schema_location.q: Does changing schema_location cause a reprocess?
source_config.schema_location.a: Yes — moving it loses the stream's checkpoint identity, so the pipeline reprocesses everything after a redeploy. Restore the original path, or accept a one-time full reprocess.

source_config.schema_location.q: What happens if schema_location is inside the ingested directory itself?
source_config.schema_location.a: Never point it inside the directory being ingested — the checkpoint/schema files themselves become input files Auto Loader tries to read, corrupting ingestion. Keep it in a separate `_schemas/` location as the auto-derived default does. See docs/02 §2.

source_config.source_catalog.q: What error appears if source_catalog is missing on a zerobus flow?
source_config.source_catalog.a: Onboarding rejects it: `source_config.source_catalog: is required but was missing or empty`, since it is required whenever `source_type` is `zerobus`.

source_config.source_catalog.q: Does source_catalog need three-part qualification itself?
source_config.source_catalog.a: No — it is just the catalog name segment; it is combined with `source_schema`/`source_table` at runtime into a fully-qualified `catalog.schema.table` string (`read_zerobus_source`), so keep it a bare catalog identifier, not a dotted path.

source_config.source_catalog.q: Does source_catalog choice affect ingestion cost?
source_config.source_catalog.a: Negligible — it only resolves which table the Delta streaming reader attaches to; cost is driven by the actual table's change volume and `max_bytes_per_trigger`, not by the catalog name.

source_config.source_catalog.q: What happens if source_catalog/schema/table point at a table this same pipeline also publishes?
source_config.source_catalog.a: That would create a genuine self-read graph edge (a fully-qualified three-part name on a table the pipeline itself writes is a sibling reference, not an escape hatch) — Lakeflow's self-read guard applies exactly as it would to a `dlt.read`. Point `zerobus` sources at genuinely external tables.

source_config.source_schema.q: What happens if source_schema is left out on a zerobus source?
source_config.source_schema.a: Onboarding rejects it: `source_config.source_schema: is required but was missing or empty`, required whenever `source_type` is `zerobus`.

source_config.source_schema.q: Is source_schema the Unity Catalog schema or a Kafka-style topic namespace?
source_config.source_schema.a: It is the Unity Catalog schema segment of the existing Delta table being streamed — combined into `source_catalog.source_schema.source_table` — not a messaging-system concept, since Zerobus here means streaming an existing Delta table.
Negligible — like `source_catalog`, it only participates in resolving the qualified table name for the Delta streaming reader.

source_config.source_schema.q: What happens if source_schema resolves to a schema this dataflow group doesn't have READ access to?
source_config.source_schema.a: Not validated at onboarding — verify at runtime; the reader will fail with a permissions error from Unity Catalog when the stream actually attempts to attach to the table.

source_config.source_table.q: What happens if source_table is missing on a zerobus flow?
source_config.source_table.a: Onboarding rejects it: `source_config.source_table: is required but was missing or empty`, required whenever `source_type` is `zerobus`.

source_config.source_table.q: Does source_table need to be fully qualified with catalog and schema?
source_config.source_table.a: No — it is just the bare table name; it is combined with `source_catalog`/`source_schema` into the qualified name by the reader, so a dotted `catalog.schema.table` string here would be wrong.

source_config.source_table.q: Does source_table's size affect the initial stream startup cost?
source_config.source_table.a: Yes, indirectly — Delta streaming from a table with a long history (many versions) can affect how much state/log the stream processes on first attach, especially combined with `starting_version`; use `starting_version`/`max_bytes_per_trigger` to bound the initial catch-up.

source_config.source_table.q: Can source_table be a table that this same pipeline group also ingests via autoloader elsewhere?
source_config.source_table.a: The Single-Read DAG mandate keys identity per `(path/table, execution mode)` — a genuinely external Delta table streamed via Zerobus is a distinct external read from an unrelated Auto Loader path, so this is fine as long as it is not the same physical table read twice under the same mode.

source_config.source_zip_handling.delete.q: What happens to the source archive if delete_source_after_extract is left unset?
source_config.source_zip_handling.delete.a: Absent means today's default: delete this run's own archive immediately after a successful extract (equivalent to `{"action": "delete_now"}`), per both the validator docstring and the schema description's stated default.

source_config.source_zip_handling.delete.q: Can I still use a plain boolean instead of the action object for delete_source_after_extract?
source_config.source_zip_handling.delete.a: Yes -- both spellings are first-class and neither is deprecated. `true` normalizes to `delete_now` and `false` to an internal-only `never`, via `archive/zip_utils.py::resolve_zip_delete_policy`.

source_config.source_zip_handling.delete.q: Does delete_after_x_days scan every archive on every run?
source_config.source_zip_handling.delete.a: It runs an age-based sweep of `source_zip_path` at extraction time on every run, removing archives matching `zip_file_pattern` older than `days` -- proportional to files in that directory, not a one-time cost, but not flagged as expensive either.

source_config.source_zip_handling.delete.q: What if extraction fails partway -- does delete_after_x_days still remove that archive?
source_config.source_zip_handling.delete.a: No -- the sweep explicitly skips any archive whose extraction failed in that same run, so a failed extraction is never swept out from under a retry, per the validator docstring.

source_config.source_zip_handling.delete.q: Is days required when action is delete_after_x_days?
source_config.source_zip_handling.delete.a: Yes -- `check_int(..., required=True, minimum=0)` runs only for `delete_after_x_days`; a sweep with no threshold isn't a policy, per the validator docstring, so onboarding rejects it if `days` is missing.

source_config.source_zip_handling.delete.q: Is days: 0 a valid value, and what does it mean?
source_config.source_zip_handling.delete.a: Yes, `days: 0` is legal and means sweep everything already committed -- the validator's `minimum=0` allows it, and the docstring explicitly mirrors this to `retention_days: 0`.

source_config.source_zip_handling.delete.q: Does a small days value increase how often the sweep runs?
source_config.source_zip_handling.delete.a: The sweep itself runs every extraction-time pass regardless of the `days` value; a smaller value just widens which archives qualify for removal, not how often the check executes.

source_config.source_zip_handling.delete.q: What happens if I set days alongside action: delete_now?
source_config.source_zip_handling.delete.a: Rejected -- the validator errors with '`{path}.days`: only meaningful for action '\''delete_after_x_days'\'', but action is '\''delete_now'\''' because it would be silently inert, which reads as a working configuration but is not one.

source_config.source_zip_handling.enable.q: What happens if I leave source_config.source_zip_handling.enabled out of my spec entirely?
source_config.source_zip_handling.enable.a: `source_zip_handling` is optional at the top level, but once you supply the block `enabled` itself is required inside it -- the validator rejects a `source_zip_handling` object with `enabled` missing. Omit the whole block if you have no ZIP/gzip pre-processing to do.

source_config.source_zip_handling.enable.q: Does enabled: false still require the other source_zip_handling fields?
source_config.source_zip_handling.enable.a: No. `source_zip_path`, `zip_file_pattern`, `target_volume_path` and the decryption sub-blocks are only checked when `enabled` is true; the validator's own branch (`if zip_handling.get("enabled")`) skips all of them otherwise.

source_config.source_zip_handling.enable.q: Does turning on source_zip_handling cost anything for an unencrypted, unzipped file?
source_config.source_zip_handling.enable.a: Yes -- if the file needs no unzip and no decryption, enabling this block still buys a staging copy for nothing; docs/02 section 5 and the member_format tip both say an unencrypted `.gz` needs no handling at all since Spark decompresses it natively on read.

source_config.source_zip_handling.enable.q: Is source_zip_handling available for zerobus sources?
source_config.source_zip_handling.enable.a: No. It is shared by `autoloader` and `asn1` only; `zerobus` streams an existing Delta table with no landing-zone file to unzip, so the block has no meaning there. See docs/02 section 5.

source_config.source_zip_handling.member.q: What container format is assumed if member_format is not set?
source_config.source_zip_handling.member.a: Default is `zip` -- the only pre-v1.7.4 behaviour: a real archive with a member table, opened by pyzipper. This is stated in both the JSON schema description and docs/02 section 5's table.

source_config.source_zip_handling.member.q: What exact values does member_format accept and what happens with an unsupported one?
source_config.source_zip_handling.member.a: Only `zip` and `gzip` (`ALLOWED_SOURCE_MEMBER_FORMATS`). Per the v1.7.4 attribute delta, an unsupported value is rejected verbatim as: 'source_config.source_zip_handling.member_format '\''tar'\'' is not supported (known formats: ['\''gzip'\'', '\''zip'\''])'.

source_config.source_zip_handling.member.q: Is there any performance difference between zip and gzip member_format?
source_config.source_zip_handling.member.a: Not documented as a performance concern either way; the distinction is structural, not a cost one -- `zip` has a member table, `gzip` is a single stream with no such table, so pyzipper can only open the former.

source_config.source_zip_handling.member.q: Can I set member_format to gzip and also set an archive password via secret_passphrase?
source_config.source_zip_handling.member.a: No -- rejected. A gzip stream has no archive-level password, so `pre_extraction_decryption.secret_passphrase` under `member_format: gzip` fails onboarding with: 'an AES password on a ZIP archive, meaningless for member_format '\''gzip'\'' (a gzip stream has no password)'. Use `pre_extraction_decryption.type` for an outer envelope instead.

source_config.source_zip_handling.member.q: Do I need source_zip_handling at all for a plain unencrypted .gz file?
source_config.source_zip_handling.member.a: No -- an unencrypted `.gz` needs no ZIP handling whatsoever. Spark and Auto Loader decompress gzip natively on read; turning this on just adds a staging copy for nothing. Use `member_format: gzip` only when the `.gz` is wrapped in something Spark cannot read through, i.e. encrypted (`.csv.gz.gpg`).

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Is passphrase_secret.secret_catalog required for pgp_symmetric, and what error do I get if it's missing?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: Yes -- under `type: pgp_symmetric`, `passphrase_secret` is called with `required=True`, and `check_secret_ref` in turn requires `secret_catalog`; a missing value fails onboarding with an 'is required but was missing or empty' error.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Is passphrase_secret the same field whether type is pgp or pgp_symmetric?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: Same three-level shape (`secret_catalog`/`secret_schema`/`secret_key`), but different meaning: under `pgp_symmetric` it is the passphrase the message itself was encrypted with (required); under `pgp` it merely unlocks the private key above (optional).

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Does resolving passphrase_secret.secret_catalog twice (for two flows) cost more?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: Negligible -- each flow resolves its own reference independently as a single secret lookup; there's no documented caching or extra cost from reuse across flows.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Can passphrase_secret and secret_passphrase be confused with each other?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: Yes, easily -- they are different secrets despite the near-identical name. `passphrase_secret` unlocks the OpenPGP layer (message passphrase under `pgp_symmetric`, or private-key unlock under `pgp`); `secret_passphrase` is the unrelated AES password on the ZIP archive itself. Never inline either as a literal.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: What happens if passphrase_secret.secret_key is left blank under pgp_symmetric?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: Rejected -- `check_secret_ref(..., required=True)` requires `secret_key` as a non-empty string; a blank value fails onboarding for `type: pgp_symmetric`.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Can I put the literal passphrase string directly as secret_key instead of a secret name?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: No -- `secret_key` is only the name of a Unity Catalog secret, resolved at runtime; the Spec Builder additionally blocks `passphrase` as a forbidden literal key name so an inline passphrase is never accepted here.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Is there a performance cost difference between a short and long passphrase_secret.secret_key value?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: Negligible -- it is just a lookup name string; the resolution cost is a single `dbutils.secrets.get` call regardless of the key name's length.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: What if the secret_key value points at a secret that doesn't exist?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: Not validated at onboarding -- verify at runtime. `resolve_secret_value` raises `SecretResolutionError` when the catalog/schema/key doesn't exist or isn't resolvable, after trying the classic-scope fallback.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Is passphrase_secret.secret_schema required under type pgp (asymmetric)?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: Only if `passphrase_secret` is supplied at all -- under `pgp` the whole block is optional, but once present, `check_secret_ref` requires `secret_schema` (and the other two fields) same as any secret ref.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Does secret_schema support dots or hyphens for nested schema names?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: No -- `assert_safe_identifier` deliberately disallows `.`/`-` even though UC schema names permit more characters, closing off SQL-injection risk since these values get spliced into DDL/error labels.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Does secret_schema resolution add noticeable pipeline runtime?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: Negligible -- it is part of the same single `dbutils.secrets.get` call as `secret_catalog`/`secret_key`; there is no separate schema-level lookup.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: What happens if secret_schema is right but rotation changed the underlying secret value?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: Not validated at onboarding or by this framework -- secret rotation is a Unity Catalog concern; the framework always resolves the current value via `dbutils.secrets.get` at run time, so a rotated value is picked up automatically on the next resolution with no framework-side caching documented.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Is private_key_secret.secret_catalog required for type pgp?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: Yes when `type` is `pgp` -- `check_secret_ref(..., required=True)` validates the whole `private_key_secret` block including `secret_catalog`, which is itself required inside a supplied secret ref.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: What is the three-level shape expected for private_key_secret?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: `{secret_catalog, secret_schema, secret_key}` -- a Unity Catalog three-level secret reference, resolved via `dbutils.secrets.get(catalog=, schema=, key=)`, never a classic workspace scope (`check_secret_ref` in spec_validator.py).

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Does resolving private_key_secret.secret_catalog add runtime overhead?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: Negligible -- it is a single UC secret lookup per pipeline run/update, not per row; the cost is a fixed secret-resolution call, not proportional to data volume.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Can I set private_key_secret when pre_extraction_decryption.type is pgp_symmetric?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: No -- rejected. Under `pgp_symmetric` the validator errors: '`private_key_secret`: not valid for type '\''pgp_symmetric'\'' -- a passphrase-encrypted OpenPGP message has no recipient keypair. Use type '\''pgp'\'' for a key-encrypted message.'

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: What error appears if private_key_secret.secret_key is missing under type pgp?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: It is required inside a supplied `private_key_secret` block -- `check_secret_ref` calls `check_string(..., required=True)` on `secret_key`, so a missing value fails with an 'is required but was missing or empty' error at that path.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Is secret_key just the UC secret name, or does it include the key material?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: It is only the UC secret name -- the third segment of `catalog.schema.key` -- resolved at runtime via `dbutils.secrets.get(catalog=, schema=, key=)`. The private key material itself lives in Unity Catalog, never in the spec.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Does grants checking for secret_key add latency to onboarding?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: No -- onboarding only validates shape (non-empty string), not that the secret exists or that the caller has grants. Grant/permission failures surface at runtime as a `SecretResolutionError`, not at onboarding.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: What if the caller lacks READ SECRET grants on this secret_key at runtime?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: `resolve_secret_value` raises `SecretResolutionError` naming the qualified `catalog.schema.key` label; this is a runtime permissions failure and is not validated at onboarding -- verify at runtime.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Is private_key_secret.secret_schema required, and what if I skip it?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: Yes, required whenever `private_key_secret` is supplied -- `check_secret_ref` requires all three of `secret_catalog`, `secret_schema`, `secret_key`; omitting any one fails onboarding with a missing-field error.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Is secret_schema case sensitive?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: The framework's own identifier guard (`assert_safe_identifier`) only allows `[A-Za-z0-9_]` and treats the value literally -- it does not fold case, so `Security` and `security` are different schema names to `dbutils.secrets.get`.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Does splitting the private key secret across secret_catalog/secret_schema/secret_key cost extra lookups?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: No -- all three segments are combined into one `dbutils.secrets.get(catalog=, schema=, key=)` call; it is a single resolution, not three.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: What happens if secret_schema is correct but the metastore has UC secrets disabled?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: The UC lookup raises `UC_SECRETS_NOT_ENABLED`, and `resolve_secret_value` falls back to a classic workspace scope, trying `catalog.schema`, `catalog_schema`, `schema`, then `catalog` in that order with the same `secret_key`. See docs/05 section 4.2.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: What if secret_passphrase is omitted entirely?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: It is fully optional at every level -- absent means the ZIP archive itself has no AES password, i.e. a plain ZIP. `_validate_pre_extraction_decryption` only checks it `if config.get("secret_passphrase") is not None`.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Is secret_passphrase a top-level ZIP setting or nested under type?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: It sits directly under `pre_extraction_decryption`, as a sibling of `type` -- not nested inside `type: pgp`/`pgp_symmetric`. It is independent of, and combinable with, the PGP layer above.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Does using secret_passphrase alongside PGP decryption double the decryption cost?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: It adds one more resolution and one more decrypt step (PGP-decrypt the envelope, then AES-unlock the ZIP), proportional to file size; not flagged as a documented performance concern beyond that extra pass.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Can secret_passphrase be set when member_format is gzip?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: No -- rejected. A gzip stream has no archive password, so setting `secret_passphrase` under `member_format: gzip` fails onboarding: 'an AES password on a ZIP archive, meaningless for member_format '\''gzip'\'' (a gzip stream has no password)'.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: If I set secret_catalog and secret_schema for secret_passphrase but forget secret_key, what happens?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: Rejected -- once `secret_passphrase` is supplied, `check_secret_ref` requires all three fields including `secret_key` as a non-empty string; a missing one fails onboarding.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Does secret_passphrase.secret_key name the archive password itself or a UC secret?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: It names a Unity Catalog secret holding the AES password on the ZIP archive -- resolved by pyzipper at extraction time -- never the literal password inline.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Is there overhead from resolving a ZIP archive password on every extraction?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: Negligible -- one secret lookup per archive extraction, not per row or per member; cost does not scale with archive contents.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Is secret_passphrase.secret_key the same secret as decrypted_columns[].secret.secret_key or encrypted_columns[].secret.secret_key?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: Not necessarily -- they are independent secret references that happen to share the same three-field shape (`check_secret_ref`). One protects the ZIP archive; the others protect AES-encrypted column values. Point them at the same UC secret only if you intend to reuse one key across concerns.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: What's the effect of leaving secret_passphrase.secret_schema unset while secret_catalog is set?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: Rejected -- `check_secret_ref` validates `secret_passphrase` as a whole object once present, requiring `secret_schema` alongside `secret_catalog` and `secret_key`; a partial secret ref fails onboarding.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Can secret_passphrase.secret_schema be an empty string to mean 'no schema'?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: No -- `check_string` treats `None` or `""` as missing when `required=True`, so an empty string is rejected the same as an absent field, not accepted as a no-op.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Does the three-level namespace (secret_catalog/secret_schema/secret_key) for the ZIP password affect extraction speed?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: No -- it is resolved once per archive via a single `dbutils.secrets.get` call; the namespace depth does not add measurable overhead.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: What happens if secret_schema is misspelled and doesn't match any real UC schema?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: Not validated at onboarding -- verify at runtime. The UC lookup fails and, on a metastore with UC secrets enabled, there is no classic-scope fallback attempted for a genuinely wrong schema name; `resolve_secret_value` raises `SecretResolutionError`.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: What happens if pre_extraction_decryption.type is left out?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: Omit `type` when the file has no outer decryption layer at all -- the block is fully optional, and `_validate_pre_extraction_decryption` no-ops when the whole config is `None` or `{}`.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: What are the only two legal values for pre_extraction_decryption.type?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: `pgp` and `pgp_symmetric` (`ALLOWED_PRE_EXTRACTION_DECRYPTION_TYPES`), checked via `check_string` with `allowed_values` -- any other value fails with an 'invalid value ... allowed values are' error.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Is PGP decryption before extraction expensive?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: Not documented as a performance concern in the validator or docs; it runs once per landed archive before the ZIP is opened, on the raw bytes -- cost scales with file size, same as any decrypt-then-read step.

source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.q: Why can't type just be a shared optional secret instead of two enum values?
source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_ex.a: 'pgp' and 'pgp_symmetric' decrypt two structurally different OpenPGP messages (PKESK vs SKESK packets) that cannot open each other, so this is one mutually-exclusive select rather than an optional extra secret on a single type.

source_config.source_zip_handling.source.q: What error do I get if source_zip_path is missing while ZIP handling is enabled?
source_config.source_zip_handling.source.a: Onboarding rejects it: `check_string` runs with `required=True`, so a missing or empty `source_zip_path` fails with an 'is required but was missing or empty' style error at that path.

source_config.source_zip_handling.source.q: Can source_zip_path point at a single ZIP file instead of a directory?
source_config.source_zip_handling.source.a: No -- it must be a directory. The validator docstring is explicit: `source_zip_path` is a landing directory, never a single file, because a real landing zone accumulates more than one archive between updates.

source_config.source_zip_handling.source.q: Does the size of source_zip_path's directory affect onboarding time?
source_config.source_zip_handling.source.a: Negligible -- onboarding only checks that the field is a non-empty string; it does not list or scan the directory. Runtime listing cost is a pipeline-execution concern, not an onboarding one.

source_config.source_zip_handling.source.q: Can two ingestion flows share the same source_zip_path with different retention or zip settings?
source_config.source_zip_handling.source.a: No -- more than one distinct `landing_retention_policy` or `source_zip_handling` regime across flows sharing the same source path is rejected, per schema comment (20): both are destructive, path-scoped side effects, so two regimes on one directory is a data-loss race.

source_config.source_zip_handling.target.q: What happens if target_volume_path is left blank on an enabled ZIP handling block?
source_config.source_zip_handling.target.a: It is required when `enabled` is true, checked with `check_string(..., required=True)`; omitting it fails onboarding with a missing/empty-field error.

source_config.source_zip_handling.target.q: Does target_volume_path need to exactly match source_config.path?
source_config.source_zip_handling.target.a: Yes, but nothing enforces it: the docs/02 sample states `source_config.path must equal target_volume_path`, and the tip is explicit that nothing validates that they agree -- a mismatch is a silent runtime failure, not an onboarding rejection.

source_config.source_zip_handling.target.q: Is there a performance cost to using a separate target_volume_path from source_zip_path?
source_config.source_zip_handling.target.a: Negligible at onboarding; at runtime the extraction step writes one copy of each member to this directory before ingestion reads it, which is an unavoidable extra write for any ZIP/gzip pipeline, documented as the handover point between extraction and ingestion.

source_config.source_zip_handling.target.q: What happens if target_volume_path and source_config.path point at different directories?
source_config.source_zip_handling.target.a: Extraction reports success, but ingestion reads zero rows while the update still reports SUCCESS -- the reader watches an empty directory. This is called out as the single most common silent misconfiguration in ZIP flows; make the two paths identical.

source_config.source_zip_handling.zip_fi.q: What happens if zip_file_pattern is omitted when source_zip_handling is enabled?
source_config.source_zip_handling.zip_fi.a: It is required whenever `enabled` is true; the validator calls `check_string(..., required=True)` and onboarding rejects the flow with a missing/empty-field error if it is absent.

source_config.source_zip_handling.zip_fi.q: Is zip_file_pattern a regex or a glob, and is it case sensitive?
source_config.source_zip_handling.zip_fi.a: It is a glob, matched the same way `file_pattern`/`pathGlobFilter` selects ingested files (e.g. `orders_*.zip` or `*.zip`), per the validator docstring. Matching is filesystem-glob semantics, so case sensitivity follows the underlying storage, not a documented framework override.

source_config.source_zip_handling.zip_fi.q: Does a broad zip_file_pattern like *.zip slow down extraction?
source_config.source_zip_handling.zip_fi.a: It can pick up more archives per run than intended, but the cost is proportional to files matched, not the pattern itself -- there is no documented per-pattern overhead beyond scanning `source_zip_path` for matches.

source_config.source_zip_handling.zip_fi.q: Does zip_file_pattern apply to the extracted files too, or only the archives?
source_config.source_zip_handling.zip_fi.a: Only to the archives in `source_zip_path`. The extracted files in `target_volume_path` are picked up by `source_config.path`/`file_pattern` for ingestion -- a separate, unrelated pattern. See docs/02 section 5's note distinguishing `zip_file_pattern` from top-level `file_pattern`.

source_config.starting_version.q: What happens if starting_version is not set on a zerobus source?
source_config.starting_version.a: No `startingVersion` option is applied at all — the code only sets it `if source_config.get("starting_version") is not None`, so the stream uses Delta's own default starting point (typically the latest/current version at first attach).

source_config.starting_version.q: Should starting_version be a quoted string like 'latest' or a plain integer?
source_config.starting_version.a: The onboarding schema types it as an integer (a specific Delta table version number). The docs example shows `"starting_version": "latest"` as a string, which is a different literal Delta reader keyword — check the type your onboarding form actually sends before assuming both spellings validate the same way.

source_config.starting_version.q: Does starting_version at 0 vs a recent version change initial load cost?
source_config.starting_version.a: Yes materially — starting from an early version means the stream catches up through every intervening Delta version before reaching current state, which is far more expensive than starting near the latest version. Pair with `max_bytes_per_trigger` to bound the catch-up rate.

source_config.starting_version.q: What happens if starting_version points at a version that has already been vacuumed?
source_config.starting_version.a: Not validated at onboarding — verify at runtime; a `VACUUM`-removed version will fail the stream at startup since Delta can no longer reconstruct that snapshot.

source_config.table.q: What happens if source_config.table is missing?
source_config.table.a: Onboarding rejects the flow -- `check_string(config.get("table"), ..., required=True)` fails when `type` is `table` (the default), since `table` is the only supported identity for a reconciliation source.

source_config.table.q: Does source_config.table need to be a three-part name, and does it support {{catalog}} templating?
source_config.table.a: Yes, a fully-qualified `catalog.schema.table` string, and it supports `{{catalog}}`/`{{env}}` template variables resolved at onboarding time, e.g. `{{catalog}}.bronze.table`. It must resolve to a real Delta table -- runtime double-checks via `DESCRIBE TABLE EXTENDED`.

source_config.table.q: Does the size of source_config.table's table matter for reconciliation cost?
source_config.table.a: It drives the cost directly: reconciliation matches via a single-column hash-key join, so a wider `compare_columns` list costs the same as a narrow one at join time, but table row count still drives the join and the Phase 1 fingerprint scan. Setting `hash_precomputed: true` where valid avoids a full re-hash pass over this table's rows.

source_config.table.q: Can source_config.table point at a table produced by this same pipeline in pipeline mode?
source_config.table.a: It is required to, in pipeline mode -- V-CYC-1 rejects a `pipeline`/`pipeline_audit_only` flow whose `source_config.table` does not resolve to an in-spec `ingestion_flows[]`/`transformation_flows[]` target of the same dataflow group, because the point of pipeline mode is comparing this update's own freshly-written rows, not an external, always-stale read.

source_config.task_run_id_column.q: What happens if source_config.task_run_id_column is not set?
source_config.task_run_id_column.a: The `task_run_id` job parameter stays correlation-only (written into log rows for traceability) but filters nothing on this side -- the pre-v1.3.0 behaviour. This is fully backward compatible; no error.

source_config.task_run_id_column.q: What column name should I use for task_run_id_column?
source_config.task_run_id_column.a: The recommended value is `__framework_pipeline_run_id`, since `dq/quarantine.py::add_quarantine_columns` stamps it on every row of every framework-materialized table and it survives onto downstream tables. It is not hardcoded -- a third-party table's equivalent column can be named anything.

source_config.task_run_id_column.q: Does setting task_run_id_column slow down the source read?
source_config.task_run_id_column.a: It narrows the read via a simple `df.filter(F.col(task_run_id_column) == task_run_id)` applied immediately after read and before `filter_condition` -- this reduces, not increases, the rows scanned downstream, and the filter itself is negligible cost.

source_config.task_run_id_column.q: Can source_config.task_run_id_column be used when execution_mode is pipeline?
source_config.task_run_id_column.a: No -- rejected on presence, because a Lakeflow update exposes no stable per-update key (`pipelines.id` is the pipeline id, constant across every update), so the narrowing would match every row that pipeline ever wrote -- a silent no-op. Use `filter_condition` instead, or keep `execution_mode: job`.

source_config.type.q: What happens if source_config.type is left unset?
source_config.type.a: It defaults to `table` (`config.get("type", "table")` in the validator), which is the only legal value anyway, so omitting it is equivalent to writing it explicitly.

source_config.type.q: Can source_config.type be set to file or sink like ingestion sources?
source_config.type.a: No. As of v1.3.0 reconciliation is scoped to Delta tables only; any other value is rejected outright: 'reconciliation is supported for Delta tables only -- type must be 'table', got '<value>'. Read the file/sink output into a Delta table first, then reconcile against that table.' See docs/07 section 7.

source_config.type.q: Does source_config.type table have any cost implication?
source_config.type.a: Negligible by itself -- it is a scope check, not a read strategy. But scoping to Delta tables is what makes the hash-key join and file-skipping affordable in the first place: a raw file/sink path could never carry precomputed hash columns or a transaction boundary.

source_config.type.q: Does the runtime re-check source_config.type even after onboarding accepts it?
source_config.type.a: Yes -- `dataset_reader.py::read_reconciliation_dataset` has a defense-in-depth check for a hand-edited control-table row, and it also resolves the table's provider via `DESCRIBE TABLE EXTENDED` and raises if it is a non-Delta provider (e.g. Parquet/CSV external tables or foreign catalogs), even though `type: table` alone doesn't prove Delta. See docs/07 section 7.

source_database.q: What happens if source_database is not provided?
source_database.a: Nothing functional — it is purely descriptive metadata stored in the control table, never validated or read by the engine. It is optional and has no default beyond being absent.

source_database.q: Does source_database need to match a real Unity Catalog schema name?
source_database.a: No — it is free text (e.g. `example_landing_db`), stored as-is; it has no relationship to `target_catalog`/`target_schema` and is not cross-checked against anything.

source_database.q: Does setting source_database affect pipeline runtime at all?
source_database.a: None — it is stored in the control table purely for documentation/observability purposes and never touched by the DAG-building or execution code.

source_database.q: Is source_database used anywhere in observability views or dashboards?
source_database.a: It feeds descriptive metadata in control tables generally, per docs/00 §Flow identity; check `docs/17_framework_observability_and_genie.md` if you need the exact observability view column it surfaces in — verify the specific view mapping at runtime if unsure.

source_description.q: What happens if source_description is left blank?
source_description.a: The target Delta table simply gets no `COMMENT`, or an empty one — it is optional descriptive metadata with no required-field error.

source_description.q: Can source_description contain single quotes or other characters that might break the table COMMENT DDL?
source_description.a: It supports `{{catalog}}` and `{{env}}` template placeholders, resolved via a plain raw-text `.replace()` over the whole spec at onboarding time before parsing — avoid embedding unescaped single quotes, since the value ultimately lands inside a SQL `COMMENT '...'` string.

source_description.q: Does a long source_description affect anything at runtime?
source_description.a: Negligible — it is stored once as the target Delta table's COMMENT metadata, not evaluated per row or per micro-batch.

source_description.q: Does {{env}} in source_description get resolved the same way as {{catalog}}?
source_description.a: Both are substituted at onboarding time by `substitute_environment_placeholders`, a literal string replace over the raw spec text — so both tokens resolve identically wherever they appear in the document, not just inside this field.

source_inputs.q: Is source_inputs mandatory on a transformation flow?
source_inputs.a: Not for the validator: `_validate_source_inputs` returns silently when the list is absent. Without inputs, `transformation_sql` can only name fully qualified tables, which bypasses the read-once source plane for external tables. Declare every upstream as an input so the binding is planned.

source_inputs.q: What shape does each source_inputs entry take?
source_inputs.a: An object with `input_name` and `table` (both required), optional `is_streaming`, `watermark` and `decrypted_columns`. Any other key is rejected: `reject_unknown_keys` runs with `ALLOWED_SOURCE_INPUT_KEYS`. In particular there is no `alias` key; `input_name` is the SQL identifier.

source_inputs.q: Do two inputs naming the same table read it twice?
source_inputs.a: No. Since v1.5.0 an input view is an alias over the read-once source plane: both inputs bind to one base node and share a single external read, per the Single-Read rule. See docs/03 §1.

source_inputs.q: What happens when an input names a table this same dataflow group publishes?
source_inputs.a: It becomes a real graph edge (`dlt.read` or `dlt.read_stream` on the sibling dataset) rather than a second scan, so Lakeflow orders the flows for you. Streaming such an input is only legal when the producer is append-only; a MERGE-written or fully recomputed producer is rejected by the streaming-read guard.

source_inputs[].input_name.q: What if an input has no input_name?
source_inputs[].input_name.a: Onboarding rejects it: `transformation_flow[<id>].source_inputs[<n>].input_name: is required but was missing or empty`. The name is the `dlt.view` the SQL reads from, so there is no default.

source_inputs[].input_name.q: Does input_name have to be a valid SQL identifier?
source_inputs[].input_name.a: It is used verbatim as the view name and in `FROM <input_name>`, so keep it to letters, digits and underscores. The validator checks only for a non-empty string; a name with spaces or dashes fails at graph definition, not at onboarding.

source_inputs[].input_name.q: Does input_name influence how much data is read?
source_inputs[].input_name.a: No. It labels a binding; the read itself is planned once per source identity and execution mode regardless of how many names point at it.

source_inputs[].input_name.q: Can two transformation flows in one spec both call an input `ord`?
source_inputs[].input_name.a: No. `_validate_no_duplicate_input_names` rejects it: `'ord' is already used by transformation_flow[<other>] ... input_name must be unique across all transformation_flows in this spec`, because every input is registered as a pipeline-wide view under its literal name.

source_inputs[].is_streaming.q: What does an input do when is_streaming is not set?
source_inputs[].is_streaming.a: It defaults to `false` (`input_config.get("is_streaming", False)` in `transformation/inputs.py`): a batch bind, a point-in-time snapshot of the table on every update.

source_inputs[].is_streaming.q: Can I write is_streaming as the string "true"?
source_inputs[].is_streaming.a: No. `check_bool` rejects a quoted value; use the JSON boolean `true`. In YAML, `true` without quotes.

source_inputs[].is_streaming.q: When is a streaming input cheaper than a batch one?
source_inputs[].is_streaming.a: For an append-only source that grows continuously: the stream reads only what arrived since the last checkpoint, while a batch bind rescans the whole table each update. For a small dimension table the batch read is simpler and costs little.

source_inputs[].is_streaming.q: Why does is_streaming: true fail on a table produced by an SCD1 flow?
source_inputs[].is_streaming.a: A MERGE-written, snapshot-applied or fully recomputed producer cannot be streamed; the source plane raises `Consumer '<id>' requested a streaming read of '<table>', which is ... cdc_load_strategy=... / target_type=...`. Set `is_streaming: false` for that input. A materialized view is rejected the same way (`a materialized view cannot be read with dlt.read_stream`).

source_inputs[].table.q: Can I leave table empty and rely on input_name alone?
source_inputs[].table.a: No. `table` is `required=True`; the error is `...source_inputs[<n>].table: is required but was missing or empty`. The input has nothing to bind to without it.
